summary: Quarterly check-in focused on usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incident, and roadmap alignment. Customer is evaluating moving latency-sensitive routes to Redwood Dedicated and wants deeper security artifacts before committing. Agreement to run benchmarks and share detailed pricing scenarios.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park (CSM): Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, we have about 55 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya Lopez (Customer): Maya here.
[00:12] Evan Chen (Customer): Evan, present.
[00:15] Priya Singh (Customer): Priya.
[00:18] Tom Alvarez (Customer): Tom on.
[00:20] Kiran Rao (Customer): Kiran.
[00:22] Lena Martin (AE): Lena from Redwood.
[00:24] Samir Patel (SE): Samir from SE.
[00:28] Jordan: Cool, agenda: usage/costs, reliability review, Dedicated & sizing talk, security docs, and next steps. If you want anything added now speak up.
[00:40] Tom: That covers it.
[00:42] Jordan: Great. Starting with usage — overall tokens up about 28% quarter-over-quarter, mostly due to the new summarization route in product search. Maya, is that aligned with what you saw?
[00:55] Maya: Yeah that's right. The search summarizer rolled out mid-September and adoption climbed in October. We did see a few power users who drive a lot of long-context calls.
[01:05] Jordan: Cool. Lena, quick note on cost: we've broken down by route and model. The summarizer route is responsible for ~46% of token spend despite being 18% of calls.
[01:20] Lena: Right — largely because of long contexts and repeated retries. Also some of the calls are using the non-quantized variant.
[01:30] Evan: On retries — we have a frontend retry policy that fires on 504s, and that doubled calls during the Oct 26 incident.
[01:40] Jordan: Let's jump to that incident. Samir, can you summarize?
[01:45] Samir: Sure. On Oct 26 at ~10:43am UTC we observed a transient throttling spike on a couple of host pools. Latency increased from steady 120ms to 900-1200ms for about 7 minutes, which triggered client-side retries. Root cause was a scheduling pressure in the autoscaler for one region, combined with an unfortunate batching spike when multiple large-context requests landed simultaneously. We rolled traffic to a healthy pool and scaled up reserved capacity.
[02:15] Priya: We saw about 2.3k failed requests and our SLO alerting fired. Can you confirm audit logs for that window?
[02:25] Samir: Yes, we have request traces and we will share the filtered audit log slice. The logs show the retry patterns and the autoscaler decisions. There was also a small mismatch in our KV cache warmup which exacerbated the CPU utilization on the hosts.
[02:45] Kiran: You said KV cache warmup — is that the key-value cache for decoder state? We sometimes see it referred to as K V cash in ops notes.
[02:55] Samir: (laughs) Yeah that's the transcription. It's the KV cache for attention state. Warmup was cold for some shards which meant larger initial compute per request.
[03:05] Jordan: What were the mitigations and long-term fixes?
[03:10] Samir: Short term we shifted traffic and bumped burst capacity. Long term we patched the autoscaler threshold logic, added a knob to pre-warm KV cache for scheduled batches, and we're recommending a Dedicated pool for the most latency-sensitive routes so you avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[03:25] Maya: That sounds good. For our priority routes we care most about 95th percentile latency under 300ms.
[03:35] Samir: Understood — that is achievable with Dedicated plus kernel/quantization tuning. We'll run a 95p benchmark on your exact request distribution.
[03:45] Jordan: On costs — moving to Dedicated shifts pricing to reserved capacity plus lower per-token execution cost. Lena, can you give a back-of-envelope?
[03:55] Lena: Sure. Based on current sustained throughput, a small Dedicated pool with autoscaling would reduce per-token compute cost by roughly 18-25% compared to hosted burst rates, but you'd have a monthly reservation. We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:13] Evan: Important: our finance team needs a 3-yr TCO comparison including potential savings from quantized model variants.
[04:22] Lena: We'll include a TCO sheet with quantization scenarios (8-bit, 4-bit) and the expected quality delta.
[04:30] Priya: On security: we need SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration details, audit log retention, and data residency answers for EU customers. Are those available?
[04:40] Jordan: Yes. We'll send SOC2 and our security one-pager in a secure link. For customer-managed keys we support KMS integration via our Private deployment and Dedicated can be configured with KMS support for encryption at rest.
[04:55] Priya: Also need details on RBAC and token-level access controls so we can map to our internal roles.
[05:03] Samir: We have RBAC docs and examples for token scoping. We'll redact customer-specific info and share examples.
[05:12] Maya: On roadmap alignment — we have a deadline for January to finalize the expansion for our EU rollout and we want Dedicated in EU to meet latency/residency. Can Redwood meet that?
[05:24] Lena: We can support Dedicated in the EU, but lead time depends on capacity commitments. If you commit to a reserved capacity by Dec we can provision targeted pools before Jan. We'll outline capacity options.
[05:36] Tom: Any risks if we keep hosted for now and only move a couple of priority routes to Dedicated?
[05:42] Samir: That's a common pattern — hybrid routing. You can pin latency-sensitive routes to Dedicated and keep bursty/less-sensitive routes on hosted. We recommend prefix caching and not changing model variants across routes to avoid cache misses.
[05:55] Kiran: We also want a technical deep dive on how batching impacts latency for single-turn long-context calls. Can we schedule a session?
[06:05] Samir: Absolutely. I'll propose a 90-minute SE deep dive where we replay your workload against Dedicated hardware profiles and show KV cache warmup behavior.
[06:15] Jordan: On actionables: Samir will run 95p latency benchmarks and collect traces. Jordan will send QBR slides + per-route cost. Lena will draft Dedicated pricing scenarios. Priya will share EU residency constraints.
[06:30] Priya: One more quick question — audit log retention: can we get 12 months of immutable logs?
[06:38] Samir: We provide configurable retention up to 13 months for audit logs on Dedicated/Private, and you can export to your SIEM. We'll include the export playbook.
[06:48] Evan: For the benchmarking, what data do you need from us?
[06:52] Samir: A sample of request distribution (anonymized), typical sequence lengths, and a list of priority routes. We don't need raw PII; anonymized request metadata is fine.
[07:02] Maya: We'll prepare that by Nov 7.
[07:06] Jordan: Great. Anything else from the customer side?
[07:10] Tom: Can you also include the model quantization quality evals? People want to see a small eval set showing rouge/accuracy deltas.
[07:18] Samir: Yes, we'll run lightweight evals — share a small eval corpus and we'll run comparisons for 8-bit / 4-bit variants.
[07:28] Jordan: Closing — recap of next steps and dates: deck & cost spreadsheet by Nov 6, SOC2/docs by Nov 7, benchmarks started week of Nov 10 with results by Nov 12, Dedicated pricing proposal by Nov 14.
[07:45] Maya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:48] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links. End call.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mis-hearings ("K V cash" instead of KV cache, model names truncated) and some speaker labels were manually corrected.
